title: The Principles of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance is a psychological phenomenon describing the mental discomfort experienced by an individual who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values, or when their actions conflict with their established beliefs. This state of internal inconsistency creates psychological tension that the human mind is naturally motivated to reduce or eliminate.

To alleviate this uncomfortable tension, individuals will unconsciously adjust their cognitions until a sense of harmony is restored. The resolution typically involves modifying one of the conflicting elements—either changing the behavior to align with the belief, altering the original belief itself, or adding entirely new consonant beliefs that justify the discrepancy.

For example, knowing that smoking is harmful (Belief A) while continuing to smoke (Behavior B) creates dissonance. An individual might resolve this not by quitting, but by downplaying the evidence ('My grandfather smoked and lived to 90') or introducing a justification that outweighs the risk ('Smoking helps me relieve stress, which is better for my heart anyway').
